item.title: eBPF rootkits and the Volatility blind spot in Linux memory forensics
item.description:
New Volatility 3 plugin exposes eBPF rootkits by walking kernel memory structures directly, bypassing syscall manipulation used by advanced Linux malware like LinkPro to hide from bpftool and live system analysis.
eBPF rootkits exploit kernel primitives designed for security monitoring: • Traditional LKM rootkits required unsigned modules (loud), eBPF runs in kernel VM via bpf() syscall (stealthy) • LinkPro hides via sys_bpf interception + magic packet activation (TCP window size 54321) • Suspicious helpers: bpf_override_return (getdents tampering), bpf_probe_write_user (userspace memory writes) • Plugin walks prog_idr radix tree in memory dump, extracts program names/types/helpers for classification
Real-world examples demonstrate operational maturity: • TripleCross: backdoor activation, process injection, execution hijacking via eBPF • Pamspy: credential harvesting through PAM uprobes without kernel modules • LinkPro: layered hiding (kernel-level + userspace fallback via /etc/ld.so.preload)
Memory forensics regains advantage over live analysis. Acquire memory via hypervisor/cloud snapshots before trusting live tools. Run `vol.py linux.ebpf_programs --dump` to extract JIT binaries for disassembly.

• **Detection IOCs**: Microsoft kit relay uses Node.js UAs (`node`, `axios`, `undici`) from cheap hosting ASNs. Google variant shows impossible travel patterns across multiple ASNs with `token.authorize` events for Chrome client

item.title: Telegram evidence beyond the cloud
item.description:
New comprehensive guide reveals critical gaps in Telegram evidence collection: most valuable artifacts exist on-device, not in cloud responses. Legal requests yield only identity data, while message content requires local database extraction.
Key technical findings: • Android cache4.db and iOS db_sqlite store unencrypted messages locally, even from "secret chats" • WAL files retain deleted messages for 1-2 days (regular chats) vs minutes (secret chats) • Desktop tdata files persist despite in-app cache clearing, often containing months of artifacts • iOS extraction requires endianness discipline: key fields use big-endian, value fields use little-endian
Critical timing factors: • Secret chat recovery window extremely narrow - acquisition delay directly impacts yield • Telegram's 2024 policy shift enables legal requests for criminal cases, returning phone/IP only • Provider responses include identity attribution but zero message content across jurisdictions
DFIR practitioners should prioritize volatile WAL artifact preservation in first 60 minutes. Parse cache4.db messages table with teleparser for TL serialization. For iOS, validate constructor IDs in binary scans to avoid false positives.
